name: Neel Kunjur
profile: Former SpaceX avionics engineer who co-founded K2 Space in 2022 with his brother Karan (CEO) to build large, high-power satellite buses for a post-Starship world. K2 raised $250M led by Redpoint at a ~$3B valuation in 2025 and sells ~20 kW satellites for a fraction of legacy prices, building 80%+ in-house.
interesting_fact: K2's thesis came from Neel noticing at SpaceX that satellites were getting smaller and cheaper (and lower-powered) just as rockets were getting bigger, so he proposed building a big, cheap satellite for medium Earth orbit.
deep_cut_fact: Before K2 he helped develop and integrate avionics for Dragon spacecraft at SpaceX and served as a Mission Director; K2 has since reimagined reaction wheels, high-voltage power and 20 kW electric propulsion under him.
notes: Brother Karan is the public face/CEO; Neel has appeared on Payload's Valley of Depth podcast ('Engineering Mass Abundance', Sept 2025) - good prep material: https://payloadspace.com/?p=30879

name: Massimo Andreasi Bassi
profile: Italian engineer ('Max') who co-founded sleep-tech company Eight Sleep in 2014 with Matteo Franceschetti and Alexandra Zatarain (YC S15), after working as a senior software engineer at Upsight. As CTO he leads the hardware/AI stack behind the Pod temperature-controlled mattress cover; Eight Sleep is valued around $2B.
interesting_fact: CEO Matteo Franceschetti has called him the 'AI and data genius' of the company; in 2026 he presented Eight Sleep's China launch in Shenzhen, its biggest market entry.
deep_cut_fact: Eight Sleep's very first product demo - a 'pajama party' showing off a passive sensor-laden mattress cover - was held at Max's house in San Francisco.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Franceschetti is the usual media voice. Fortune (Aug 2026) covered Eight Sleep's FDA/health push. Hardware lessons blog with the co-founders: https://www.ycombinator.com/blog/lessons-on-building-hardware-from-the-founders-of-eight-sleep

name: Hiroki Koga
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Oishii (vertical-farming strawberries, Jersey City NJ)
profile: Japanese-born Keio graduate and former consultant (Deloitte Japan) who worked with leafy-green plant factories before founding Oishii in 2016 while doing his MBA at UC Berkeley. Oishii grows premium Omakase strawberries indoors using bee pollination and robotics, has raised $200M+ and is valued around $1B.
interesting_fact: He deliberately skipped leafy greens and chose strawberries - 'the holy grail of vertical farming' - reasoning that if you can grow strawberries indoors you can grow anything, and that a premium crop funds cost reduction.
deep_cut_fact: As a boy he spent three years of elementary school in France, where people were excited about Japan (Pokemon, Toyota) - a contrast to the 'gloomy outlook' he heard at home that shaped his drive to export Japanese farming craft; he calls vertical farming his 'ikigai'.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (Milken, Advertising Week Climatech) - energy angle: indoor farming is power-intensive, relevant to the podcast's energy theme.

name: Dr. Graham Sills
current_role: Co-founder & Director of AI, Luminance (Cambridge/London legal AI)
profile: Cambridge mathematician who co-founded Luminance in 2015 with Adam Guthrie, building AI that reads, reviews and now negotiates legal contracts. He leads Luminance's AI/R&D; the company (CEO Eleanor Lightbody) is backed by March Capital, National Grid Partners and Slaughter and May and is valued around $1B.
interesting_fact: Luminance's 'Panel of Judges' approach combines multiple specialised AI models (a mixture of experts) to cross-check legal analysis - the 'Legal-Grade' AI that Sills' R&D team builds.
notes: Very low public profile; CEO Eleanor Lightbody is the media face. A search summary said Luminance's bio gives him a PhD in computational number theory from Trinity College, Cambridge, but I could not verify it on a primary page (web-search budget ran out). Route via Tancredi PR.
